name: Integrity
question: Are the parts one connected object, free of real interpenetration, with every part a single body?
inputs: declared joints (parent, child, origin) for connectivity and joint-pair exclusion
steps: Preprocess with prepare(): unitless designs are scaled by s = ref_diag / max(design_diag, 1e-9) about (XY bbox centre, min z); unitless or front_declared=False designs are rotated in place by the yaw in {0,90,180,270} maximising fscore@0.05 against the reference (6000 samples each). Joint origins and axes are transformed with the parts, and prismatic limits are scaled by s (fixed 2026-09-14).

Voxelise every part at res = 0.004 m (surface samples, hit cells, binary_fill_holes); build the pair table of touching pairs with deep_m3 = |core_a ∩ core_b|·res³ and collides = deep_m3 > 1e-6 ∧ deep_m3/min(vol) > 0.10.
nonjoint = pair rows with joint_pair False; pen_frac = Σ_nonjoint deep_m3 / max(Σ vol_i, 1e-12).

cfree = 1 − |nonjoint rows with collides| / max(|nonjoint|, 1); collision_frac_sweep counts nonjoint rows with deep_m3 > 1e-6 and frac_of_smaller > f for f in (0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25), reported only.
edges = every pair row plus each joint (parent, child) with origin non-null and max(surface_distance to parent, to child) ≤ 0.02 m; components by union-find, sorted by volume.
largest_frac = vol(largest component) / Σ vol; connected_part_frac = |largest component| / n_parts.
whole_i = 1 if the part's filled grid has ≤ 1 26-connected component, else 1 iff exactly one component holds ≥ 5% of its cells; whole_body_rate = mean(whole_i).
shells = parts with filled_frac = 1 − shell_count/count < 0.05; lowest_z_m, below_ground_m, lifted_m reported only.
status: fail if largest_frac < 0.95 or connected_part_frac < 0.90 or pen_frac > 0.10; else degraded if any shell-only part; else pass. Empty design: fail, 0.

constants.COLLIDE_FRAC: 0.10 — collision share of the smaller part
constants.CONTACT_JOINT_TOL_M: 0.02 m — joint origin distance to both parts that connects them
constants.LARGEST_COMPONENT_FAIL: 0.95 — largest-group volume share below which 1.1 fails
constants.CONNECTED_PARTS_FAIL: 0.90 — largest-group part share below which 1.1 fails

golden: floating_part (n_components > 1), interpenetration (n_colliding > 0), joint_origin_off_boundary (joint_issue > 0), via analysis.summarize, not evaluate() (golden.py:40-57, 72-77).
limitations: Touch tolerance is one dilated 4 mm cell (about 4–10 mm); thin parts are over-counted.
pen_frac divides by the sum of part volumes, so overlap is double-counted in the denominator.
Overlap between declared joint pairs is excluded from collisions however deep; joint_pair_overlap_cm3 is reported only.
Open meshes stay shells: volumes under-counted and status degraded (the reference itself is degraded).
Ground penetration and lift are not scored.

name: Stability
question: As one rigid body of uniform density on flat ground, how far can the largest connected group tilt before its centre of mass passes the support edge?
inputs: 3D part meshes (voxel occupancies of the largest 1.1 component)
steps: Preprocess with prepare(): unitless designs are scaled by s = ref_diag / max(design_diag, 1e-9) about (XY bbox centre, min z); unitless or front_declared=False designs are rotated in place by the yaw in {0,90,180,270} maximising fscore@0.05 against the reference (6000 samples each). Joint origins and axes are transformed with the parts, and prismatic limits are scaled by s (fixed 2026-09-14).

Voxelise every part at res = 0.004 m (surface samples, hit cells, binary_fill_holes); build the pair table of touching pairs with deep_m3 = |core_a ∩ core_b|·res³ and collides = deep_m3 > 1e-6 ∧ deep_m3/min(vol) > 0.10.
main = largest connected component from 1.1; band = max(0.005, 0.01·(z range of all parts)).
com = Σ centroid_i·vol_i / Σ vol_i over main; pts = kept surface samples of main.
Support set = pts with z ≤ z0 + band (z0 = min z); H = XY convex hull; h = max(com_z − z0, 1e-6).
For 720 azimuths u: d(u) = max_{p∈H} u·p − u·com_xy, angle(u) = atan2(d(u), h) in degrees; critical_tilt_deg = min angle, tilt_direction_deg = argmin.
support_margin_m = min d(u); support_margin_norm = margin / √(hull area/π); n_support_vertices = |H|.
score: score = clip(critical_tilt_deg / tilt_ref, 0, 1); without tilt_ref, 1 if critical_tilt_deg > 0 else 0
status: fail if critical_tilt_deg ≤ 0; degraded if n_support_vertices ≤ 2 (pose_sensitive) or the design has > 1 connected component; else pass. Empty design: fail, 0.
golden: com_outside_support (tilt < 0); all other scenes must keep tilt > 0; via summarize with band 0.005 on all parts (golden.py:50-53, 181-182).
limitations: Statics only; no settling simulation; joints are not moved.
Uniform density = voxel volume, so shell-only parts weigh almost nothing.
Floating parts are excluded from the body but set the band height.
Support set uses surface samples (≤ 60000 per part), not voxels.
A lifted main group is not penalised; stability above the reference caps at 1.

name: Geometry
question: Is the design the reference's size and shape, and do its declared parts sit in chair-like configurations?
inputs: reference meshes, roles, bounds, joint prismatic_range
steps: Preprocess with prepare(): unitless designs are scaled by s = ref_diag / max(design_diag, 1e-9) about (XY bbox centre, min z); unitless or front_declared=False designs are rotated in place by the yaw in {0,90,180,270} maximising fscore@0.05 against the reference (6000 samples each). Joint origins and axes are transformed with the parts, and prismatic limits are scaled by s (fixed 2026-09-14).
Extents: width = max(ext_x, ext_y), depth = min(ext_x, ext_y), height = ext_z; same for the reference bounds.
If not unitless: lr_k = log2(max(ext_k, 1e-6)/rext_k), size_score = 2^(−mean_k |lr_k|); within_population_p5_p95_frac = mean_k [p5 ≤ ext_k ≤ p95], reported only.
Sample 20000 area-weighted surface points of design (seed 0) and reference (seed 1); _center_ground both (XY bbox centre → reference XY centre, min z → 0).
fscore: da, db = nearest-neighbour distances both ways; P = mean(da < τ), R = mean(db < τ), F = 2PR/(P+R), τ ∈ {0.02, 0.05}; chamfer = (mean da + mean db)/2.
Best yaw over {0,90,180,270} is reported (best_yaw_deg, front_consistent); the scored term is f0 = fscore@0.05 as oriented.
seat_height: top = max seat z; range [rtop, rtop + max_j prismatic_range_j[1]] over all reference joints; out = distance outside range; score = max(0, 1 − out/0.15).
backrest_above_behind_upright: mean of [back z-centre > seat z_max − 0.02], [back y-centre > seat y-centre], [back z-extent ≥ back y-extent].

wheel_round_horizontal_axle: roundness = best over 3 PCA axes of max(0, 1 − (std/mean of 36-bin max radius)/0.2); axle_horizontal = [|axis_z| < 0.5]; score = 0.5·mean roundness + 0.5·mean axle_horizontal.
column_vertical: mean |z-component| of the largest-variance eigenvector of each gas-lift part's vertices.
ground_contact_points (always): n = 8-connected clusters of vertices with z ≤ zmin + 0.01 on a 3 cm XY grid; score = min(n, 5)/5.
armrests_both_sides: |{sign(armrest x-centre − seat x-centre)} ∖ {0}| / 2.
score: score = mean(size_score [metric designs only], f0 fscore@0.05, mean(role predicate scores))
status: always pass for a non-empty design; empty design: fail, 0.

constants.SEAT_DECAY_M: 0.15 m — seat height distance outside range that scores 0
constants.ground clusters: 3 cm cell, 1 cm band, reference n = 5

golden: none; LEXICON_CASES pins role names the predicates read (golden.py:107-129).
limitations: Scored F-score is as oriented; a design facing the wrong way loses shape score although best yaw is reported.
Population ranges are not scored; unitless designs have no size term (oracle scale).
Seat range uses the largest prismatic travel of any reference joint.
Extra ground clusters are not penalised; armrest sides use sign of x only.
Predicates exist only for declared roles and are chair-specific.

name: Kinematics
question: Do the declared joints realise the claimed motions and the reference articulation, and can each joint move through its range without collision?
inputs: declared joints (type, parent, child, axis, origin, limits)
claims K (moving_part, relative_to, joint_type, axis text, range text)
reference joints (type, axis, origin, prismatic_range, roles) and bounds
steps: Preprocess with prepare(): unitless designs are scaled by s = ref_diag / max(design_diag, 1e-9) about (XY bbox centre, min z); unitless or front_declared=False designs are rotated in place by the yaw in {0,90,180,270} maximising fscore@0.05 against the reference (6000 samples each). Joint origins and axes are transformed with the parts, and prismatic limits are scaled by s (fixed 2026-09-14).

Voxelise every part at res = 0.004 m (surface samples, hit cells, binary_fill_holes); build the pair table of touching pairs with deep_m3 = |core_a ∩ core_b|·res³ and collides = deep_m3 > 1e-6 ∧ deep_m3/min(vol) > 0.10.
moving = joints with type ≠ fixed and both endpoints present; rigid groups = components of contact rows minus moving-joint pairs plus fixed-joint pairs.
Completeness per moving joint: [(ball ∨ ‖axis‖ > 0) ∧ origin ≠ None ∧ (continuous ∨ ball ∨ limits ≠ None)]; declaration_completeness = mean.
joint_on_boundary = mean of max(0, 1 − max(0, d − 0.02)/0.1), d = max surface distance of origin to parent and child; reported only.

Claims: kids = parts strictly matching moving_part; for each kid and each moving joint whose child rigid group contains it, q = rs·(0.4·type_score + 0.4·axis_score + 0.2·range_score), rs = 1 if the parent group strictly matches relative_to else 0.5; claim score = mean over kids of best q (0 if no kids); claims_recall = mean over K.
type_score = 1 if equal else TYPE_COMPAT; axis_score = max(0, 1 − err/45°) with err = acos|a_z| (vertical) or asin|a_z| (horizontal), 1 if no requirement, 0 if no axis.
range_score: continuous joint → 1 if claim is full ('continuous'/'360'/'freely') or requires revolute/continuous else 0.5; no limits → 0.5 (0.25 if full); full → min(1, span/2π); else [span > 0].

Reference match: Q[a,b] = role·(0.35·ts + 0.35·ax + 0.3·org), role = 0.5·[child roles meet child group] + 0.5·[parent roles meet parent group or none] (0 if child fails), ts = max type_score vs type and alt_type, ax = max(0, 1 − angle/45°), org = max(0, 1 − dist/(0.25·ref_diag)).
Hungarian assignment maximising ΣQ; tp = Σ matched Q (> 0); recall = tp/|ref joints|, precision = tp/|moving|, reference_f1 = 2PR/(P+R).

Sweep (first 24 moving joints): moving set = BFS from child over contacts and other joints, not through the parent; samples = 11 angles 2πk/12 (continuous or unlimited revolute), 8 over limits (revolute, prismatic), 8 offsets + 11 angles (cylindrical); ball or no axis/origin → ratio 0.
At each sample re-voxelise the moving parts; blocked if Σ max(0, deep overlap − rest overlap)·res³ > max(1e-6, 0.05·moving volume); ratio = free/n; achievable_range_ratio = mean ratio.
score: score = mean(claims_recall or 0, reference_f1, achievable_range_ratio, declaration_completeness or 0)
status: skipped (None) iff declares.joints is false and no joints exist; fail if no moving joints (score still computed); else pass; no degraded. Empty design: fail, 0.

constants.ORIGIN_SCALE_FRAC: 0.25 — origin error normaliser, fraction of reference diagonal
constants.claim weights: 0.4 type / 0.4 axis / 0.2 range; parent factor 1 or 0.5

golden: joint_origin_off_boundary (2 cm rule) and blocked_sweep, but golden measure re-implements the sweep (child only, 1e-6 m³ threshold) and does not call evaluate() (golden.py:55-64, 78-91).
limitations: Joints are swept independently; coupled mechanisms are not sampled jointly; only the first 24 joints are swept.
ratio counts free samples anywhere in the range, not the range reachable from rest; unlimited prismatic joints sample only offset 0.
welded_by_contact and joint_on_boundary are reported, not scored.
A claim's score is diluted over every part with the moving role (five wheels need five joints).
Axis and range requirements are keyword tests on claim text.

name: Operability
question: Can a user operate the design (grip, reach, pass)?
steps: Not built: the dimension is written with status not_built and no metrics.
status: always not_built; absent from the empty-design record.
limitations: Operability probes (grip, reach, pass) are not built.

name: Decomposition
question: Does the design have the claimed parts, in reference-like counts and granularity, under recognisable names?
steps: Canonicalise roles with the task lexicon: strip parentheticals, first conjunct, drop positional words, singularise, longest synonym match (ties: later end).
Per P: c = canon(part), acc = ACCEPT.get(c, {c}); n = Σ design counts over acc; need = max(1, max reference count over acc); score = min(n, need)/need; coverage = mean.
hist = max(0, 1 − Σ_k |design_k − ref_k| / max(Σ ref_k, 1)).
gran = 2^(−|log2(n_parts / max(n_ref_parts, 1))|).
unrec = #(parts with a role whose canon is None) / n_parts.
consolidation_violations = touching non-joint pairs with the same canonical role and material; reported only.
part_iou_vs_reference_volume_weighted: design shifted to reference XY centre and z = 0, 1 cm voxels, best IoU per reference part weighted by its cell count; reported only.
score: if roles declared or any role present: mean(coverage or 0, hist, gran, 1 − unrec); else gran
status: pass when roles exist; degraded otherwise (only granularity is measurable), with score = gran. Empty design: fail, 0.
golden: check_lexicon: 10 real names and strict/broad caster matching (golden.py:107-129); no scene for the 3.1 formulas.
limitations: Granularity penalises too many parts as much as too few.
A single mesh representing several parts counts once.
Part IoU has no yaw search and is not scored; ref_occ is computed and unused (evaluate.py:652).
The lexicon is one hand-written table per task.

name: Aesthetics (computed)
question: Is the form mirror-symmetric and proportioned like the reference?
steps: Preprocess with prepare(): unitless designs are scaled by s = ref_diag / max(design_diag, 1e-9) about (XY bbox centre, min z); unitless or front_declared=False designs are rotated in place by the yaw in {0,90,180,270} maximising fscore@0.05 against the reference (6000 samples each). Joint origins and axes are transformed with the parts, and prismatic limits are scaled by s (fixed 2026-09-14).

Voxelise every part at res = 0.004 m (surface samples, hit cells, binary_fill_holes); build the pair table of touching pairs with deep_m3 = |core_a ∩ core_b|·res³ and collides = deep_m3 > 1e-6 ∧ deep_m3/min(vol) > 0.10.
Take all filled cell centres, centre them at their mean, quantise on a 1 cm grid.
For plane normals at 0, 5, …, 175° in XY: mirror M = Q − 2(Q·n)n, quantise, IoU = |base ∩ mirror| / |base ∪ mirror|; symmetry_iou = best.
prop = 2^(−mean(|log2((H/W)/(H_r/W_r))|, |log2((D/W)/(D_r/W_r))|)) with W = max horizontal extent, D = min.
status: always pass (depth computed+adjudicated, but no adjudicated input is used here). Empty design: fail, 0.
limitations: Mirror planes pass through the voxel centroid; the offset is not fitted.
Proportion cannot tell which horizontal axis is the width.
Designs more symmetric than the reference cap at 1.

name: Creativity
question: How far is the design from the reference, and how much of it is catalogue versus created parts?
steps: novelty_1_minus_fscore@0.05 = 1 − f0 fscore@0.05 (as oriented).
distinct_pool_parts = number of distinct pool ids; pool_instances_by_origin = instance counts by origin kind (reference, standard, same_type, other_type).
created_instances = parts with source kind created; created_frac = created_instances / n_parts.
Diversity across seeds is attached at report time (see 'diversity').
status: pass for a non-empty design; absent for an empty design.
limitations: Novelty is 1 − similarity, so a broken design reads as novel.
Origin counts are instance counts.

name: Material
question: Are declared materials present, plausible per role against the reference and population, and does the design carry a 75 kg sitter with their densities?
steps: Resolve each material name case-insensitively to a LIBRARY submaterial id → (submaterial, class, density), else None.
cov = Σ volume of resolved parts / Σ volume.
Claim groups = one class set per material word in material claims; claim_class_coverage = groups met by any design class / groups (reported, used by A1).
agree = volume-weighted share of role-bearing parts whose class equals the reference's most common class for that role.
like = volume-weighted mean of p(class | role) / max_k p(k | role), p = (count + 1)/(Σ count + 9) over population counts; unresolved = 0.
mass_i = density_i·vol_i; if seat parts and Σ mass > 0: loaded tilt = critical tilt of the main group with these masses plus 75 kg at (seat bbox XY centre, seat max z), band as in 1.2.
lscore = max(0, loaded)/loaded_tilt_ref (or [loaded > 0] without reference; 0 if not computed).
score: score = mean(cov, like or 0, agree or 0, min(1, lscore))
status: skipped if declares.materials is false and no part has a material; else pass if cov > 0.99, fail if cov = 0, degraded otherwise. Empty design: fail, 0.

constants.OCCUPANT_KG: 75 kg — point load at the seat top

limitations: Densities are Artiverse medians; open-mesh volumes and masses are under-counted.
Names that do not resolve to a library id count as undeclared.
Agreement uses the reference's majority class only; claim class coverage is not in the score.
The occupant is a point mass.

name: Assembly
question: Can the parts be placed in the declared order along straight collision-free paths with every prefix supported and standing?
steps: Preprocess with prepare(): unitless designs are scaled by s = ref_diag / max(design_diag, 1e-9) about (XY bbox centre, min z); unitless or front_declared=False designs are rotated in place by the yaw in {0,90,180,270} maximising fscore@0.05 against the reference (6000 samples each). Joint origins and axes are transformed with the parts, and prismatic limits are scaled by s (fixed 2026-09-14).

Voxelise every part at res = 0.004 m (surface samples, hit cells, binary_fill_holes); build the pair table of touching pairs with deep_m3 = |core_a ∩ core_b|·res³ and collides = deep_m3 > 1e-6 ∧ deep_m3/min(vol) > 0.10.
order = sequence parts that exist; coverage = |set(order)| / n_parts.
Per step, candidates = [declared direction] + the six axis directions; the first step is always feasible.

For each candidate d: shift the part's grid by round(−d·t) cells for t = 1, 3, 5, … up to int((bbox diagonal + 0.05)/res) + 1; blocked if deep overlap with the union of placed parts exceeds its rest overlap + 2 cells.
insertion_feasible = any candidate unblocked; declared_direction_feasible = declared candidate unblocked (reported only).
supported = every contact component of placed parts contains a part with min z ≤ design zmin + 0.01.
stable = critical tilt of all grounded placed components as one body (band 0.005) > 0; 0 if nothing grounded.
score: score = mean(coverage, mean insertion_feasible, mean supported, mean stable)
status: no sequence: fail with 0 if declares.sequence, else skipped; otherwise pass if coverage = 1, else degraded. Empty design: fail, 0.
golden: unsupported_first_step (supported_prefix_frac < 1), via a re-implementation in measure (golden.py:66-68, 92-103).
limitations: Insertion paths are straight translations along the declared direction or the six axes.
Joints do not count as support.
A 2-cell stride can pass 1-cell obstacles.
Infeasible steps never fail the dimension.

name: Function
question: For each claimed subsystem: are its parts present, placed where the reference places them, and linked (through a moving joint when motion is carried)?
inputs: contact rows and all declared joints
steps: Role centres = mean bbox centre per canonical role, normalised to the design bounds (design) or reference bounds (reference).
presence = mean over named parts of [some part satisfies the name, broad matching].
placement = mean over named parts with centres in both of max(0, 1 − ‖design centre − reference centre‖/0.5); 0 if none.
Adjacency = contact rows plus every declared joint (no origin test); moving pairs = non-fixed joints.

connection per link: A, B = parts strictly matching from/to; BFS ≤ 4 hops scores 1 if a B part is reached (crossing a moving joint when carries = motion), 0.5 if reached without the needed moving joint, 0 otherwise or if A or B is empty.
Aggregates: mean presence, mean placement, mean connection (None → 0) over subsystems.
score: None — presence, placement and connection are reported separately
status: skipped if roles are not declared and no part has a role; else pass; absent for an empty design.
limitations: Joints connect regardless of the 2 cm rule used in 1.1.
carries = force and load are treated alike.
Bbox normalisation removes aspect ratio.
The page claims matrix averages the three numbers (site_template_v3.html:861).

name: Attribute proxies
question: Is each attribute claim satisfied, as far as a rule over computed metrics can tell?
steps: kind = material → score = 4.1 claim_class_coverage (None if 4.1 skipped).
statement contains 'desk' → score = seat_height predicate score (0 if absent).
contains 'adjust' and not 'lever' → 1 if a moving prismatic/cylindrical joint's child group contains a seat, armrest, backrest or gas lift cylinder part, else 0.
contains 'lever' → 0 without lever parts, else 0.5 + 0.5·[a lever's voxel centroid is within 0.08 m of a gas lift cylinder, swivel mechanism or seat surface].
Otherwise proxy None, score None.
score: per attribute, not combined and not folded into any dimension
status: no status field; absent for an empty design
limitations: Keyword dispatch is task-specific.
A2 tests seat height, not desk use.
A lever at any distance earns 0.5.

name: DINOv2 image similarity
question: How similar is the design's clay render to the condition photo?
inputs: clay render from the cond camera (azimuth 300°, elevation 22°, 384 px, 16 samples) of the evaluated parts
steps: Render clay views cond, iso, front, side from the parts after evaluate() (so after oracle scale and yaw).
Embed each image with facebook/dinov2-large: e = pooler_output[0] / ‖pooler_output[0]‖.
cosine = e_render · e_photo; the reference render is scored as an item too.
score: raw cosine; page shows the mean over seeds
status: no status; designs without parts have no render and no value
limitations: One fixed camera, not fitted to the photo.
Clay render versus photograph domain gap.

name: Diversity across seeds
question: How different are a system's designs from one another?
inputs: 6000 surface samples per design saved after evaluate() (<key>_points.npy)
steps: Group records by (system, tier).
For groups with ≥ 2 point sets, shift each set so its XY bbox centre is 0 and min z is 0.
For every pair: 1 − fscore@0.05; report the mean over pairs and n_seeds.
limitations: The group key omits rounds and condition, so r1/r2/r3 tool-arm records are pooled as seeds.
No yaw alignment between designs.

name: VLM · kinematics claims
question: Does the joint the rule matcher picked really realise the kinematics claim?
inputs: joint motion sheet (three poses, moving parts orange, parent blue, axis red)
steps: Per claim, pick the 2.2 best entry with q > 0 and an existing joint; render three poses (0/90/180° for continuous or unlimited revolute, lo/mid/hi for revolute and prismatic); other joint types get no sheet.
Labels L# are drawn only where the part covers ≥ 25 px in the flat ID render; first 124 parts only.
No sheet: score None if 2.2 is skipped, else 0 ('no candidate joint').
Ask the judge (temperature 0) for parts_match, type_axis_match, motion_realises_claim, physically_sensible, score 0–10, evidence.
grounded = cited labels meet (moving labels ∪ parent label) and all cited labels exist; score = score/10 if grounded else 0.
If grounded and any of parts_match, type_axis_match, motion_realises_claim is not true: score = min(score, 0.3).
score: family = mean over claims per judge; page column = mean over judges, then over seeds
status: per claim: judged / ungrounded / no candidate joint / skipped (no joints declared)

constants.zoom: moving bbox diagonal < 0.3 of design diagonal

limitations: Cylindrical and ball joints are shown turning about their declared axis; the sliding of a cylindrical joint is not shown.
physically_sensible is asked but not used.
A parse failure is ungrounded and scores 0.

name: VLM · required parts and attributes
question: Do the parts declared with each required role look like that part, and does the design satisfy each attribute claim?
inputs: materials sheet (material attributes) or clay sheet
computed facts (extent, seat top and reference range, symmetry)
steps: If no label row has a role, every P and A is skipped (score None).
Parts: candidates per P = labels whose canonical role satisfies the part (broad); one call for all P.
Part grounded = candidates non-empty ∧ answer labels meet candidates ∧ all labels exist; score = score/10 if grounded and present is true, else 0.
Attributes: one call each; grounded = at least one cited label and all cited labels exist; score = score/10 if grounded else 0; if satisfied is not true, min(score, 0.3).
score: page column = mean over judges of mean(parts mean, attributes mean), then over seeds
status: per claim: judged / ungrounded / no candidate / skipped (no roles)
limitations: Attribute grounding accepts any existing label, relevant or not.
Parts under 25 visible pixels in a view are unlabelled there.

name: VLM · design quality
question: How good is the design as an office chair, compared with the photo, from neutral clay views?
inputs: clay sheet (condition camera, front-right, front, right side)
steps: Ask for recognisable, resemblance, proportion, coherence, overall on 1–10 with written anchors, each with an observation naming a view.
Per criterion: (s − 1)/9 clipped to [0, 1]; None if not numeric.
grounded = observations with a view cover ≥ 3 distinct criteria; if not grounded every criterion is 0.
score: page column = mean over judges of the overall criterion, then over seeds; Spearman agreement between the first two judges is reported
limitations: Grounding does not check that views or observations are valid.
Absolute per-design scores drift more than pairwise preferences.
